Given your history of significant sun exposure and the classic "sandpaper-like" texture of this non-tender, scaly plaque, I suspect this is an actinic keratosis.

text: The dermoscopy was normal, which is unexpected for a scaly plaque. Let me perform a physical examination of the lesion to assess its texture and borders more closely.

Since the dermoscopy was normal and the lesion persists, I need to obtain a tissue sample to rule out squamous cell carcinoma or other proliferative disorders.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. These findings are consistent with actinic keratosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy results confirm the diagnosis of actinic keratosis, characterized by atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. I will proceed with treatment options such as cryotherapy or topical agents to prevent progression.
